data.name: SREBP1 / SREBP2
data.description: Sterol regulatory element-binding proteins 1 and 2; master transcription factors for de novo lipid and cholesterol biosynthesis. mTORC1 promotes SREBP nuclear entry (via Lipin-1 and S6K1), linking nutrient sensing to the lipogenic program. SREBP1/2 are thus a major downstream metabolic output of mTORC1 alongside protein synthesis and autophagy suppression.
data.description_beginner: Master genetic switches for building new fats and cholesterol from scratch. mTORC1 helps move them into the nucleus to switch these genes on, linking nutrient signals to fat-making, alongside its roles in protein building and blocking cleanup.

reading_levels.student: Transcription factors for lipogenic genes, activated downstream of mTORC1.
reading_levels.research: Regulated via S6K1 and Lipin-1 nuclear exclusion; the link is indirect and partly cell-type specific.

studies.finding: mTOR/SREBP1 signaling governs hepatic glucose partitioning; the insulin-responsive mTOR/SREBP1 axis promotes lipogenesis versus glycogen accumulation. studies.title: Activation of a metabolic gene regulatory network downstream of mTOR complex 1
studies.authors: Düvel K; Yecies JL; Menon S; Raman P; Lipovsky AI; Souza AL; Triantafellow E; Ma Q; Gorski R; Cleaver S; Vander Heiden MG; MacKeigan JP; Finan PM; Clish CB; Murphy LO; Manning BD

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Tsc2-/- mouse embryonic fibroblasts and other cells with rapamycin; transcriptomics, metabolomics, RNAi
studies.finding: Used cells with constitutively active mTORC1 (TSC2 loss) and rapamycin to map what mTORC1 switches on besides protein synthesis. Gene expression and metabolite profiling showed that mTORC1 activation is enough to drive glycolysis, the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway and de novo lipid synthesis. This ran through a transcriptional program of HIF1alpha and SREBP1/2 target genes; SREBP1 and 2 were needed for proliferation downstream of mTORC1, and their activation required S6K1. Boundary: cultured cells, mostly mouse fibroblasts with genetic mTORC1 activation; tissue and human relevance not tested here.

studies.title: Hepatic mTORC2 activates glycolysis and lipogenesis through Akt, glucokinase, and SREBP1c
studies.authors: Hagiwara A; Cornu M; Cybulski N; Polak P; Betz C; Trapani F; Terracciano L; Heim MH; Rüegg MA; Hall MN

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Liver-specific rictor knockout mice (LiRiKO); primary hepatocytes with constitutively active Akt2 or glucokinase rescue
studies.finding: The authors deleted rictor, an essential mTORC2 component, only in mouse liver. In fed knockout mice the liver lost Akt Ser473 phosphorylation and had lower glucokinase and SREBP1c activity, so it kept making glucose (gluconeogenesis) while glycolysis and fat synthesis fell, as if it could not sense that the animal had eaten. The mice became hyperglycaemic and hyperinsulinaemic with low blood lipids. In mTORC2-deficient hepatocytes, constitutively active Akt2 restored both glucose flux and lipogenesis, while extra glucokinase restored glucose flux but not lipogenesis, placing Akt as the main route from hepatic mTORC2 to these outputs. Boundary: Mouse liver with lifelong genetic loss of mTORC2, plus cultured mouse hepatocytes. Not a drug study and not tested in people. Drafted from the abstract only.

studies.title: Sterol regulatory element-binding proteins are essential for the metabolic programming of effector T cells and adaptive immunity
studies.authors: Kidani Y; Elsaesser H; Hock MB; Vergnes L; Williams KJ; Argus JP; Marbois BN; Komisopoulou E; Wilson EB; Osborne TF; Graeber TG; Reue K; Brooks DG; Bensinger SJ

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse T cells with Cd4-cre-driven deletion of Scap (removing both SREBP1 and SREBP2 activity), siRNA and constitutively active SREBP constructs, rapamycin and LY294002 pretreatment, ChIP for SREBP1/2 at lipogenic promoters, GC-MS lipid measurement, Seahorse profiling, LCMV-Armstrong infection and homeostatic-proliferation transfers
studies.finding: Activating T cells switch on cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis genes within hours, and this paper showed the switch runs through PI3K and mTOR to SREBP: 100 nM rapamycin given 30 minutes before stimulation blocked the induction of the lipogenic programme, prevented processing of full-length SREBP and its accumulation in the nucleus, and reduced SREBP1 and SREBP2 occupancy at lipogenic promoters to background. Deleting Scap in T cells, which removes both SREBP1 and SREBP2 activity, left thymic and peripheral T-cell numbers normal but the cells could not blast: they entered G1 and stalled, failed to raise cholesterol and fatty acids after activation, and increased ECAR and OCR only modestly where controls rose about ten-fold and four-fold. Adding cholesterol conjugated to methyl-beta-cyclodextrin roughly doubled survival at 48 hours (21 to 45 percent) and restored growth, cell-cycle entry and ER expansion, which points to cholesterol as the limiting step. After LCMV-Armstrong infection the Scap-deficient mice had fewer virus-specific CD8 T cells with lower IFN-gamma and TNF, while homeostatic proliferation was unaffected. Boundary: mouse genetics and mouse cells; the mTOR step is shown with rapamycin pretreatment in cultured T cells, and the in vivo arm measures the consequence of losing SREBP activity rather than of inhibiting mTOR.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 drives the SREBP transcription factors, which turn on the genes for making fat and cholesterol - growth needs membrane, not just protein.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 switches on SREBP, the genes that build fat and cholesterol – a growing cell needs membrane material, not just protein.
relations.boundary: Mammalian cell studies (POR2008, PET2011) and an emerging rather than settled consensus. Cultured cells; the size of the effect in whole animals and in people is not measured by these studies. KID2013 adds primary mouse T cells: rapamycin blocked SREBP processing and nuclear entry after T-cell activation, and Scap-deleted T cells could not raise sterol synthesis. Still no human tissue data.

relations.mechanism: SREBP1 is the main transcriptional switch for de novo lipogenesis, and SREBP2 for cholesterol synthesis.
relations.mechanism_beginner: SREBP is the master switch for making new fat from scratch.
relations.boundary: Mammalian cell studies and a review (POR2008, PET2011, SHI2014). SREBP's role in lipid synthesis rests on cell-based work and does not measure it in people.
